title: Amatriciana
subtitle: Roman pasta with guanciale and tomato
excerpt: The pasta of Amatrice: spaghetti in a sparse, intense sauce of guanciale or pancetta, tinned tomatoes, dry white wine, and pecorino, with no onion or garlic in the original. Deeply savoury with a clean acidity from the tomatoes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Amatriciana takes its name from Amatrice, a town in the mountains of Lazio (historically part of the Abruzzo region) that was devastated by an earthquake in 2016. The dish predates the addition of tomatoes: the older version, known as gricia, is simply guanciale, pecorino, and pasta. When tomatoes were added, the modernised dish eventually became Roman through the large Amatricean community that settled in Rome. The canonical Roman version uses spaghetti or rigatoni, guanciale (cured pig's cheek), tinned tomatoes, dry white wine, pecorino romano, and chilli flakes. No onion, no garlic: these are Roman additions. Outside Italy, pancetta is the common substitute for guanciale.

content.text: Render the guanciale or pancetta slowly so the fat melts out; it should not crisp immediately. Deglaze with wine and let it evaporate before adding the tomatoes. The sauce should cook until the tomatoes completely lose their tinned edge and the sauce is thick and slightly glossy. Toss vigorously with pasta and a little cooking water so the sauce emulsifies.

items.preparation: cut into 1 cm cubes; or guanciale
grated; use pecorino romano if available; to serve

content.text: Put the pancetta in a large cold frying pan. Set over medium-low heat and cook slowly for 8 minutes until the fat has rendered and the pieces are golden. Add the chilli flakes and cook for 30 seconds. Pour in the wine and let it bubble and evaporate, about 1 minute.

Add the crushed tomatoes. Season with a little salt (the pancetta and cheese are both salty). Simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until the sauce is thick and the tomatoes have completely broken down. Taste; adjust the salt and chilli.

Cook the pasta in well-salted water until al dente. Reserve 100 ml of pasta water. Drain. Add the pasta to the sauce and toss over medium heat for 1 minute, adding pasta water to loosen if needed. Serve with grated pecorino or parmesan and black pepper.
